title: Should Asphalt Driveways Be Sealed? Sealcoating Pros and Cons
metaDescription: Yes, if the base is sound: sealing every 2-3 years slows oxidation and water entry but cannot fix structural cracks. The pros, cons and who should skip it.
h1: Should Asphalt Driveways Be Sealed? Sealing Pros and Cons
keywords: asphalt seal coating pros and cons
sealing asphalt driveway pros and cons
intro:
Yes, most asphalt driveways should be sealed, as long as the base underneath is sound: a coat every two to three years slows the oxidation and water entry that turn blacktop gray, brittle and cracked. What sealing cannot do is repair a weak base, poor drainage or structural cracking, and that limit settles most of the argument.

Sealcoating companies make it sound essential, and skeptics call it black paint. Both have a point. This guide lays out what sealer actually does, the real benefits and drawbacks, the strongest case against it, and a simple way to decide whether your own driveway is a good candidate this year.
quickAnswer: Seal an asphalt driveway that is structurally sound, at least six to twelve months old and starting to gray, and repeat every two to three years with crack filling first. Skip it on brand-new blacktop, on a driveway that still beads water from its last coat, and on pavement with widespread alligator cracking or potholes, which needs repair rather than a coating.

sections.heading: Should Asphalt Driveways Be Sealed? The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Pro | Matching con |
| --- | --- |
| Slows oxidation and graying | Has to be renewed about every 2 to 3 years |
| Cuts water entry at the surface | Does nothing for wide cracks or a failing base |
| Some resistance to oil and gas spills | Best chemical resistance comes from coal tar, which has health and legal issues |
| Restores a dark, even look | Poor application peels, scuffs or builds up |
| Smoother surface is easier to clean | Can be slicker when wet and tracks while fresh |

Sealing is surface maintenance. It protects the top of the pavement from sun, air and water, and it does nothing for what lies beneath. On a well-built driveway, that maintenance is cheap and worthwhile. On a failing one, it is a cosmetic expense.

The rule of thumb: if water soaks into the surface instead of beading, the asphalt is graying, and cracks are few and narrow, seal it. If large areas are breaking up, put the money toward repair. If you decide to go ahead, our [best asphalt driveway sealer](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) rankings cover which pail suits which surface.

sections.heading: What Does Sealing an Asphalt Driveway Actually Do?
sections.body:
Asphalt is stone glued together with a petroleum binder. Over time, sunlight and oxygen break that binder down at the surface. It loses its oils, fades from black to gray, turns brittle and starts shedding fine particles, a process called raveling. Water then works into the more open surface, and in cold climates freeze-thaw cycles widen small cracks. That surface aging is the target of sealer.

### A thin, sacrificial layer

Driveway sealer is usually an asphalt emulsion, sometimes an acrylic and, in some areas, coal tar. It forms a fresh film over the old surface that blocks some UV, slows water penetration, resists spills to varying degrees and restores the dark color. Two coats add only a fraction of an inch, and that film wears away over two or three years of sun and traffic.

### What it cannot do

Sealer adds no strength. It does not support the pavement, repair the gravel base, fix drainage or knit together sections that have cracked through. Alligator cracking (a web of connected cracks), potholes, sunken ruts and broken edges are base problems. A coat on top improves the look for a while and nothing more.

### Why people seal their driveway

Most owners seal for a mix of reasons: to slow surface wear, to keep water out of small cracks, and because a dark, even driveway simply looks maintained. All three are legitimate, as long as expectations stop at the surface.

sections.heading: What Are the Pros of Sealing an Asphalt Driveway?
sections.body:
### It slows oxidation

The clearest benefit is protection from UV and oxygen. The film takes the sun so the binder below does not, slowing the drying-out that makes the surface brittle. Driveways in high-sun regions benefit most. Renewed every few years, the coat keeps the binder underneath more flexible and less prone to raveling.

### It cuts water entry at the surface

A fresh coat tightens the surface texture and fills hairline cracks, so less water soaks in. That matters most where freeze-thaw cycles are frequent, since water in the surface expands every cold night. Sealer will not keep water out of wide cracks, which need a proper filler, but combined with crack repair it reduces a major cause of winter damage.

### It resists spills

Gasoline and motor oil soften asphalt binder. A sealer film holds spills on the surface long enough to clean them up. Coal tar resists petroleum best, which is why it was popular for decades; asphalt emulsions and acrylics offer less resistance but still beat bare, oxidized pavement.

### It looks better and cleans easier

A freshly sealed driveway is deep black, uniform and noticeably sharper beside a lawn and walkway, which matters if the house is going on the market. The smoother film is also easier to sweep and hose off than an open, gray surface. These benefits are cosmetic, but they are a real part of why people seal.

sections.heading: What Are the Cons of Sealing an Asphalt Driveway?
sections.body:
### It never ends

A coat typically lasts about two to three years, so sealing is a recurring job for the life of the driveway. Each round means materials or a contractor bill, a weekend of work if you do it yourself, and a day or two without parking. Our guide to [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) puts numbers on that cycle.

### Bad application creates its own damage

Coating a damp or dirty surface leads to peeling. Laying it on too thick leaves soft spots and tire marks. Sealing every year builds up layers that crack and flake on their own, a pattern sometimes called map cracking. These failures are avoidable but common, and they can leave the driveway looking worse than if it had been left alone.

### It can be slicker and messier

A fresh coat can be slicker than bare asphalt when wet, especially on slopes. Many sealers contain sand or allow it to be added for traction, so look for one that does if your driveway is steep. Fresh sealer also tracks on shoes and tires for the first days and permanently marks concrete walks, garage floors and siding if you are careless.

### Coal tar carries health and legal baggage

Coal tar sealers contain high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), some classified as known or probable human carcinogens. U.S. Geological Survey studies have linked coal tar sealcoat to raised PAH levels in nearby dust and stream sediment, and several states and many local governments ban or restrict it. Asphalt emulsions and acrylics have far lower PAH content.

sections.heading: Does Sealcoating Asphalt Really Help?
sections.body:
It helps the surface, and the honest answer stops there. Some pavement engineers and highway agencies doubt that residential sealcoat makes much difference to how long a driveway lasts overall, and their argument deserves a fair hearing.

### The skeptic's case

Most driveway failures start underneath: a thin or poorly compacted base, bad drainage or tree roots. Sealer does nothing about any of them, so a driveway built on a weak base cracks on schedule whether it is sealed or not. A well-built driveway on a good base, meanwhile, can last a long time with little care. There is also relatively little independent long-term research on residential driveway sealcoat specifically, and much of the published support comes from the sealcoating industry. Anyone promising that sealer will double the life of every driveway is overselling it.

### Where that case is weaker

Surface aging is real, visible and well understood. Oxidation and raveling happen at the top, and a film that blocks UV and water slows them down. On a driveway with a sound base, keeping the top layer flexible and tight reduces the small cracks that let water reach the base in the first place. In that role, sealer plus crack filling is inexpensive maintenance.

### The fair summary

Sealer protects the surface; it does not save a bad base. If your driveway was built well and drains properly, sealing every two to three years with prompt crack filling keeps it in good shape at low cost. If the base is failing, no amount of sealer changes the outcome.

sections.heading: Which Asphalt Driveways Benefit Most From Sealing?
sections.body:
The ideal candidate is a structurally sound driveway past its first year that has started to gray. If water soaks in rather than beading, fine aggregate is showing, and cracks are few and narrow, sealer plus crack filling will slow its aging at a reasonable cost. That describes most residential driveways between roughly one and fifteen years old.

### Climate tips the balance

Driveways in hot, sunny regions face constant UV, so a protective film does useful work. Driveways in cold regions face freeze-thaw cycling, where keeping water out of the surface matters. In both, a two-to-three-year cycle tends to make sense. In mild, cloudy, low-traffic settings, the case is weaker and the interval can stretch.

### Heavy use argues for it

If cars park in the same spots, if there are occasional oil drips, or if the driveway doubles as a basketball court or play area, the spill resistance and easier cleaning are worth having.

### Selling soon

A fresh coat a few weeks before listing is a low-cost curb appeal upgrade. It will not add measurable resale value, but it signals a maintained property.

### Fill cracks first

If your driveway fits this profile, crack filling matters as much as the coating. Pick a dry, warm window; our guide to the [minimum temperature for sealing a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/) explains the air, pavement and overnight readings to check.

sections.heading: When Is Sealing an Asphalt Driveway Not Necessary?
sections.body:
### Brand-new asphalt

Do not seal blacktop in its first months. The binder is still rich in oils and the surface already sheds water. Sealing too early can slow curing and leave a coat that bonds poorly. Wait roughly six to twelve months, or one full warm season; our guide on [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/) explains the signs.

### A driveway sealed recently

If the last coat went down within a year or two, water still beads and the color is still dark, the previous coat is still working. Adding coats too often is one of the main reasons sealer gets a bad reputation.

### A failing driveway

Widespread alligator cracking, potholes, sinking or crumbling edges call for repair, an overlay or replacement. Sealing that pavement is money spent on appearance. If more than roughly a quarter of the surface shows structural cracking, have a paving contractor assess it before buying sealer.

### A different material

Gravel, concrete and paver driveways need different products. Concrete benefits from penetrating or film-forming concrete sealers rather than asphalt sealer, and pavers need joint sand and a paver sealer. If yours is concrete, the [best concrete driveway sealer](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) guide is the right starting point.

sections.heading: Is Sealing a Driveway Worth It Financially?
sections.body:
Usually, on sound pavement. Sealing is maintenance, so the comparison is against the cost of resurfacing or replacing a driveway early, which runs many times more per square foot than a coat of sealer. Even a modest extension of the surface's life can cover years of sealing at do-it-yourself prices, though the exact payoff depends on climate, traffic and how well the driveway was built.

### Where the money does the most

Crack filling delivers the best return of any line item. Water entering through open cracks is what undermines the base and leads to potholes and settling. If the budget is tight, filling cracks this year and sealing next year is a better order than sealing over open cracks.

### Where it does the least

A driveway that is already failing structurally. Sealing over widespread alligator cracking buys a season of better looks and nothing else, and the cracks are back after the first hard winter.

### The interval matters

Sealing every two to three years is where the math works. Sealing every year roughly doubles the long-run cost and builds up layers that crack and peel. A quick water test each spring tells you whether the existing coat is still doing its job.

sections.heading: If You Do Seal, Which Sealer Should You Use?
sections.body:
For most homeowners, a water-based asphalt emulsion. It is widely available, legal everywhere, low in odor and cleans up with water. Budget versions are thin and may last only a couple of seasons; premium versions with polymer, rubber or sand cost more but generally wear better.

### Acrylic and polymer-modified sealers

These often dry faster and may hold color longer, at a higher price per pail. They are a reasonable upgrade when the driveway needs to return to service quickly.

### Coal tar

It offers the strongest resistance to oil and gasoline, but it is banned or restricted in many areas over PAH concerns. Where it is legal, weigh that resistance against the health and environmental trade-offs; for a home driveway, most people are better off with an emulsion.

### Rejuvenators

Some owners of very old, oxidized driveways try rejuvenators, which aim to soak in and restore some flexibility to the binder rather than just coat it. Results depend heavily on the product and the pavement, so treat claims with caution.

### Follow the label

Whatever you choose, follow the label on coverage, temperature and cure time. A mid-priced sealer applied well outperforms a premium one applied over dust or in cold weather. The [best driveway sealer](/best-driveway-sealer/) guide compares picks for both asphalt and concrete if you are deciding between surfaces.

mistakes.title: Expecting sealer to fix structural damage
mistakes.body: Sealer is a surface coating. It cannot bridge alligator cracking, fill potholes or support a sinking base. Coating a failing driveway makes it look better for a season before the cracks show through again. Repair or resurface first, and only seal pavement that is structurally sound.

mistakes.title: Sealing every single year
mistakes.body: More coats do not mean more protection. Yearly sealing builds a thick layer that can crack and flake on its own, and it doubles the long-run cost. Seal about every two to three years, and only when a water test shows the surface absorbing water again.

mistakes.title: Skipping crack repair
mistakes.body: Water entering through open cracks does far more damage than surface oxidation. Sealing over cracks hides them briefly but leaves the path to the base open. Fill cracks wider than about 1/8 inch with a proper filler first, using backer rod in deep ones so the filler does not sink.

mistakes.title: Using coal tar without checking local rules
mistakes.body: Coal tar sealers are banned or restricted in several states and many cities and counties because of their PAH content. Applying one where it is prohibited can bring fines and raises health concerns. Check local rules, and choose an asphalt emulsion or acrylic when in doubt.

mistakes.title: Writing off sealing entirely
mistakes.body: The opposite mistake is dismissing sealer as useless. On a sound driveway in a sunny or freeze-thaw climate, a coat every few years plus crack filling slows surface aging at low cost. A surface that is never maintained oxidizes, ravels and cracks sooner than it needs to.

faqs.q: Is sealing an asphalt driveway necessary?
faqs.a: Not strictly, but it is useful maintenance for most structurally sound driveways. Sealer slows surface oxidation, reduces water entry and improves appearance. It does not strengthen the pavement or fix base problems. A well-built driveway that is never sealed will still last for years, but its surface usually grays, ravels and cracks sooner than a maintained one.

faqs.q: Does sealing a driveway really work?
faqs.a: Yes, for the surface. A fresh coat blocks UV, slows water penetration and holds spills on top long enough to clean them. It does not fix a weak base, poor drainage or structural cracking, which cause many driveway failures. On sound pavement, sealing every two to three years with crack filling is effective, low-cost maintenance.

faqs.q: What happens if you never seal your driveway?
faqs.a: The surface oxidizes, grays, turns brittle and gradually sheds fine aggregate. Small cracks form and widen faster, especially in freeze-thaw climates, letting more water reach the base. How much that matters depends on construction quality, drainage and climate. A driveway with a strong base can still last a long time, but maintenance usually extends it.

faqs.q: Does sealing a driveway make it slippery?
faqs.a: A fresh coat can be somewhat slicker than bare, textured asphalt when wet, especially on slopes. Many sealers include sand for traction, and some labels allow sand to be added. On a steep driveway or in a rainy climate, choose a sand-filled product or ask your contractor to add sand. Traction usually improves as the coat weathers.

Done badly, yes. Sealing new asphalt too soon, coating a damp or dirty surface, applying it too thick or sealing every year can cause peeling, soft spots, tire marks or a buildup that cracks. Done correctly on cured, clean, dry, structurally sound pavement, sealing does not harm the driveway and helps protect the surface.

Coal tar sealers contain high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, some classified as known or probable carcinogens. Research has linked coal tar sealcoat to raised PAH levels in nearby dust and waterways, and several states and many localities ban or restrict it. Asphalt emulsion and acrylic sealers contain far lower PAH levels and are the safer choice.

faqs.q: Should you sealcoat your driveway yourself or hire a pro?
faqs.a: Most homeowners can seal a typical driveway themselves with a squeegee, a quality sealer and careful prep, usually for well under a contractor price. Hiring out makes sense for very large or steep driveways, heavy crack repair, or if you lack the time or physical ability. Either way, confirm cleaning, crack treatment, coats and cure time.

bottomLine: Seal an asphalt driveway when the pavement is structurally sound, past its first six to twelve months and starting to gray. In that case a coat every two to three years, with cracks filled first, slows surface aging, keeps water out and keeps the driveway looking cared for at modest cost. Skip it on brand-new blacktop, on a driveway that still beads water from its last coat, and on pavement with a failing base, where the money belongs in repair. Avoid coal tar where it is restricted, apply thin coats on clean, dry pavement, and treat sealer as surface maintenance rather than a cure.
